cleanIntro: The JHP 45 is Hi-Point's .45 ACP blowback pistol, built by Haskell Manufacturing and sold under the Hi-Point name; this book covers it alongside the JCP in .40 S&W. Like the rest of the line the barrel is fixed in the polymer frame and the slide is released by driving out a slide retainer pin with a 1/8 inch punch — there is no takedown lever, and no amount of pulling on the slide substitutes for that pin. One thing differs from its bookmate: the JHP-45ACP is a nine-round pistol where the JCP-40S&W is a ten.

steps.title: Magazine out — and the disconnect proves nothing about the chamber
steps.action: Press the magazine release behind the trigger guard on the left of the frame and draw the magazine out. The JHP has a magazine disconnect that blocks the trigger linkage with the magazine gone, but it is a mechanical device and Hi-Point tells you not to lean on it. It says nothing at all about a round in the chamber. Clear the bench of loose ammunition before continuing.
steps.prose: The barrel's chamber observation port is a convenience, not a clearing check.
steps.quote: 1. Remove the magazine by depressing the magazine release button. (FIG. 1)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 1, p.25
steps.warn: Although your Hi-Point pistol has a chamber observation port, you should never rely solely on the chamber observation port or your memory to determine whether your Hi-Point pistol is loaded or unloaded. Always remove the magazine, fully retract and lock open the slide and then visually and physically (with your finger) check to make sure there is not a cartridge in the chamber.

steps.title: Thumb safety DOWN — otherwise the slide will not retract
steps.action: Push the thumb safety fully down to the off (fire) position, showing the red dot. On this pistol the rotary safety blocks sear movement and also locks the slide, so with the safety up the slide simply will not come back. It feels like a jam and it is not. Keep the muzzle in a safe direction and your finger outside the trigger guard while you do it — the chamber is still unknown.
steps.prose: Pushing it fully UP later is what will lock the slide open for you.
steps.quote: 2. Push the thumb safety fully downward to the off (fire) position. (Note: The thumb safety must be in the off (fire) position to allow the slide to retracted.) (FIG. 2)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 2, p.25

steps.title: Slide back, lock it open on the safety, then look AND feel
steps.action: Hold the frame in your firing hand with your finger off the trigger and pull the slide fully back by the rear serrations to eject anything chambered. Lock it open the Hi-Point way — thumb safety UP into the notch on the slide, then ease the slide forward until it catches on it. Now look into the chamber and the magazine well, and then check both with a fingertip. On a .45 with a dark chamber the fingertip is what settles it.
steps.prose: Safety glasses from this point: the sear assembly in this frame is spring-loaded.
steps.caution: Always wear safety glasses when disassembling your Hi-Point pistol, to protect your eyes from components that are under pressure, such as springs, and the sear assembly that could fly out and hit you.
steps.quote: 4. Lock the slide in the rearward (open) position by pushing the thumb safety/manual slide lock up into the notch on the slide and slowly releasing the slide from the fully rearward position until it locks in the open position. (FIG. 4)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 4, p.26

steps.title: Slide retainer pin out — 1/8 inch punch and a small hammer
steps.action: With the thumb safety still up in the slide notch, the slide retainer pin sits exposed at the rear of the frame. Drive it fully through and out with a 1/8 inch pin punch and a small hammer. This is the only tooled step in the strip and the pin has to come right out; leave it part way and the slide will not lift, and levering against a half-driven pin burrs the frame hole.
steps.prose: Rest the frame on something solid so the blow goes into the pin, not into the polymer.
steps.quote: 6. While the thumb safety/manual slide lock remains pushed up into the notch of the slide, the slide retainer pin at the rear of the frame will be exposed. Use a 1/8″ pin punch and a small hammer to remove the slide retainer pin from the frame by pushing it fully through and out of the frame. (FIG. 6 & 6.1)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 6, p.26

steps.title: Empty magazine in, drop the striker, magazine back out
steps.action: Press the thumb safety down so the slide runs forward. Insert an EMPTY magazine — that is what deactivates the magazine disconnect and frees the trigger — point the muzzle somewhere genuinely safe, and pull the trigger to release the striker. The gun can be stripped with the striker cocked but the slide resists all the way; released, it lifts easily. Take the magazine straight back out afterwards.
steps.prose: This is a deliberate trigger pull on a gun you have just cleared, so the muzzle direction is the whole safety margin.
steps.quote: 8. Insert an empty magazine into the magazine well to deactivate the magazine disconnect device and, with the muzzle of your Hi-Point pistol pointed in a safe direction (a safe direction is one in which no one can possibly be injured in the event of an unintentional discharge), pull the trigger to release the striker. (Note: Although it is possible to disassemble your Hi-Point pistol with the striker cocked, it is much easier to remove the slide with the striker released.) (FIG. 8)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 8, p.27

steps.title: 3/8 inch back FIRST, then lift the rear and push forward
steps.action: Finger over the rear of the slide, draw it back about three eighths of an inch, and only then lift the back of the slide and push it forward off the frame. The firing pin stands proud of the breech face on this design, so lifting before that short retraction bends it against the barrel — and the barrel is part of the frame, so it is the pin that loses. The slide travels forward off the fixed barrel rather than tilting out.
steps.prose: Once the slide is off, do not touch the trigger: the sear is exposed and spring-loaded.
steps.quote: 10. While holding a finger over the rear of the slide pull the slide approximately 3/8″ to the rear and then pull the rear of the slide up and push it forward to remove the slide assembly from the frame. You must pull the slide approximately 3/8″ to the rear to retract the firing pin from the chamber before before pulling up on the slide. The firing pin extends beyond the breach face and can be damaged if the slide is pulled up before it is retracted. (FIG.10 & 10.1)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 10, p.27
steps.warn: Do not pull trigger with the slide removed. Sear is under spring tension and could fly out.

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide rod forward out of the frame
steps.action: Pull the recoil spring and its guide rod forward out of the cylindrical channel in the frame below the barrel. On a blowback .45 that spring is stout, and it is the frame it lives in, not the slide — so it comes out of the frame, as a unit with the rod. Watch which way the rod points as it leaves: it goes back in facing forward.
steps.prose: Keep the frame upright from here; parts inside it are now exposed.
steps.quote: 11. Pull the recoil spring and recoil spring guide rod forward and out of the frame. (FIG. 11)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 11, p.28

steps.title: Retainer out of the slide, then tip the firing pin group free
steps.action: Pull the slide retainer out the back of the slide, then invert the slide and let the firing pin spring, the firing pin spring assist and the firing pin slide out of the rear. Have a hand under them. Do NOT invert the frame while you are at it — with the slide off, the frame's internals are only held in place by gravity and will drop out if you tip it.
steps.prose: That is the last part of the strip; lay the three pieces out in order.
steps.quote: 13. Turn the slide upside down and allow the firing pin spring, firing pin spring assist and the firing pin to slide out the back of the slide. (Note: Be careful not to shake or invert the frame because components are now exposed and can simply fall out). (FIG. 13)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 13, p.28

steps.title: Nine rounds, not ten — the JHP-45ACP magazine
steps.action: Know the count for your own pistol. Hi-Point's spec panel for the JHP-45ACP states a nine-shot standard magazine, where the JCP-40S&W in the same book gets ten. A .45 magazine that stops at nine is full, not faulty, and forcing a tenth round bends the feed lips. Both models are rated for +P ammunition, so pressure is not the limiter here — the case diameter is.
steps.prose: The general paragraph on page 8 of this manual says eight rounds for both models; the per-model spec panel is the model-specific figure and is the one that governs a JHP 45.
steps.caution: The shared text on p.8 says 'eight round detachable magazine' for both models — the per-model panel disagrees with it and is the model-specific statement.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 1, Main Features, MODEL JHP-45ACP spec panel, p.9

steps.title: Jacketed ammunition only, and Hi-Point rings only on the rail
steps.action: Two limits before the pistol is used again. Feed it jacketed ammunition: unjacketed lead leaves deposits in a barrel that is pressed into the frame and cannot simply be swapped out. And the accessory rail under the dust cover takes Hi-Point's own rings and nothing else — it is not a Picatinny or Weaver interface, so a light or laser mount from another maker either will not sit or will sit and shift.
steps.prose: Use only commercially manufactured ammunition meeting SAAMI, CIP or NATO standards.
steps.quote: Only use jacketed ammunition to prevent the buildup of lead deposits in the barrel.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 4, Loading, p.14
steps.warn: Accessory rail to accept Hi-Point rings ONLY.

steps.title: Barrel from the chamber end — never a rod down the muzzle
steps.action: Run a solvent-wet patch through the barrel from the chamber end several times, then a solvent-wet bristled brush back and forth, then an oiled patch, checking each until they come out clean. Cleaning from the muzzle with the slide locked back pushes fouling, oil and solvent back into the frame's mechanism, and that is where blowback pistols pick up malfunctions. Finish with dry patches until no oil comes out, unless the gun is going into storage.
steps.prose: Then brush the outside of the barrel with a nylon brush and wipe it dry — the slide rides on it.
steps.quote: As with any semi-automatic pistol, your Hi-Point pistol should be cleaned from the breach. Cleaning with the slide locked to the rear by inserting a rigid cleaning rod from the muzzle can cause dirt, oil and solvents to build up inside your Hi-Point pistol, causing malfunctions.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 8, Preventive Cleaning, p.23

steps.title: Interval — 1,500 to 2,000 rounds, and sparing lubrication
steps.action: Hi-Point's complete-clean interval for the JHP 45 is every 1,500 to 2,000 rounds, or any time the pistol gets wet or is exposed to weather. Lubricate with a lightly oiled patch on the outside of the barrel, the inside of the slide and the outside of the magazine, and stop there. A blowback action carries its recoil spring in the frame where unburned powder collects, and excess oil turns that into a paste that slows the slide.
steps.prose: While it is apart, inspect the barrel for lead build-up, bulges or cracks, and check the magazine follower springs back freely and does not catch.
steps.quote: You should completely clean your Hi-Point pistol after firing every 1,500 to 2,000 rounds or anytime it is exposed to the elements, becomes wet, etc.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 10, Complete Cleaning, p.29

steps.title: The retainer pin must be flush, or the slide is not retained
steps.action: When the pistol goes back together, drive the slide retainer pin fully home so it is flush with the frame and stands out of neither side. This is the failure the JHP will not warn you about — it still fires with the pin short, but the slide is no longer locked to the frame, and an unretained slide on a .45 blowback comes rearward under recoil. Check both sides of the frame by eye and by fingertip.
steps.prose: The slide has to be locked open on the thumb safety while the pin goes in, so its notches line up with the frame hole.
steps.quote: Always make sure that the slide retaining pin is properly reinstalled when assembling your Hi-Point pistol. If it is not correctly installed, your Hi-Point pistol will still fire, but the slide will not be properly locked in place which could lead to serious personal injury, and/or damage to your Hi-Point pistol.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 11, Assembly, p.35
steps.warn: Flush both sides. There is no other cue that the pin is short.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the frame with its integral barrel, the slide, the recoil spring and guide rod, the slide retainer, the firing pin with its spring and spring assist, and the magazine. That is the whole of the JHP 45 disassembly Hi-Point publishes and the whole of what an owner may do — the sear, its spring and the drop-safety counterweight stay in the frame, and going after them voids the warranty.
steps.prose: Reassembly is the reverse; the retainer pin and the 3/8 inch slide pull are the two steps worth slowing down for.
steps.quote: Never disassemble your Hi-Point pistol further than this procedure. Any further disassembly by untrained persons could cause your Hi-Point pistol to malfunction and will void the warranty.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL JCP 40S&W / MODEL JHP 45ACP — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document (unlike the C9/CF380 book, which carries "2019 V.02" on its page 3) — Chapter 9, Disassembly, p.28

deepAbsentReason: Hi-Point publishes no deeper teardown for the JHP 45 and forbids one: "Never disassemble your Hi-Point pistol further than this procedure. Any further disassembly by untrained persons could cause your Hi-Point pistol to malfunction and will void the warranty." (Chapter 9, Disassembly, p.28). The 13-step strip walked above IS the manual's complete disassembly, and it already reaches the firing pin, its spring and the spring assist out of the slide — further than most field strips go. What stays inside the frame is the sear and sear spring, the counterweight drop safety and the trigger linkage; the manual introduces those in Chapter 1 as design features and never as serviceable parts, and it warns twice that pulling the trigger with the slide off can throw the sear out under spring tension. There is nothing to author a deep branch from.

cleaning.name: BARREL — FROM THE CHAMBER END ONLY
tasks: Solvent-wet patch from the CHAMBER end, several times, with a cleaning rod
Solvent-wet bristled brush back and forth from the chamber end
Oiled patch through once and examined; repeat until it comes out clean
Clean dry patches until no oil remains — unless the pistol is going into storage
Nylon brush and solvent over the outside of the barrel, then wipe dry

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Nylon brush and solvent on the bottom surfaces where the slide rides on the frame
Oil-wet nylon brush on the breech face and under the extractor, slide held muzzle-down
Wipe with clean patches until they come away clean
Check the remaining exposed areas of the slide for debris
Zamak 3 slide: corrosion resistant but soft — brush it, do not scrape it

cleaning.name: FRAME & MAGAZINE
tasks: Wipe exposed frame parts with a patch slightly dampened with solvent
Wipe the magazine body and feed lips with a slightly dampened patch
Press the follower down with a fingertip and release — it must spring back without catching
JHP-45ACP standard magazine is 9 rounds; do not force a tenth

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION & INSPECTION
tasks: Complete clean every 1,500-2,000 rounds, or any time it gets wet
Lightly oiled patch on the outside of the barrel, the inside of the slide and the outside of the magazine — that is the whole lubrication
Do not over-lubricate; excess collects unburned powder and slows the slide
Inspect the barrel for lead build-up, bulges, cracks or obstructions
Inspect frame and slide for corrosion or visible damage
Do not use a cracked, bulged or obstructed barrel — contact Strassell's Machine, Inc.

reassembly: Firing pin into the rear channel of the slide, slide held muzzle-down.
Firing pin spring and firing pin assist spring into the same channel.
Slide retainer into the rear channel, rounded part first, held by the cylindrical part.
Recoil spring and guide rod into the frame below the barrel, guide rod facing FORWARD.
Index finger over the rear slide channel to hold the retainer in place; set the slide on the frame with the recoil assembly aligned to the tab at the front of the slide.
Draw the slide rearward until the retainer aligns with the hole at the rear of the frame and the firing pin is clear of the barrel, then push the slide down to lock it.
Pull the slide fully back and lock it open on the thumb safety.
Drive the slide retainer pin fully through with the 1/8 inch punch until FLUSH with the frame, protruding from neither side.
Press the thumb safety fully down to release the slide forward.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty, walk Hi-Point's function test. Insert an empty magazine and feel it lock in. Safety down, pull the slide fully back and release — the internal slide lock must hold it open. Drop the magazine, cycle the slide several times to confirm it runs freely, then lock it open on the thumb safety and press the safety down to release it. With no magazine in and the safety down, pull the trigger and confirm the magazine disconnect stops the striker. With the safety up, the trigger must do nothing, both with and without an empty magazine inserted. Finally, safety down with an empty magazine in, the trigger must release the striker. Muzzle in a safe direction throughout.
